answer_1.quote: Summarizing video content into a natural language description (i.e. 'video captioning') is a crucial aspect of video understanding.

answer_2.quote: We use the standard BLEU-4 (B-4), Rouge-L (R-L) and CIDEr metrics used in captioning tasks. We also calculate an Entity F1 (Ent. F1) score to measure how well the ground‑truth entities are covered in the generated caption.

answer_3.quote: We input the captions to LLaMA-2 LLM ask it to rate whether the caption is of high quality or not. ... The LLM rater scores the quality of captions according to the following criteria: 1) It should contain the name of important entities; 2) It should not hallucinate; 3) It should not leave out critical information.

answer_4.quote: We employ a human‑in‑the‑loop procedure for this task. First, we ask a LLM rater to score the quality of captions ... The samples that the rater flagged as not being of high quality are separated for manual verification and correction.
answer_4.guideline: Human raters check whether captions contain important entity names, avoid hallucinations, and include all critical information from the video.
